info.name: Agentic Watershed — ATProto API calls
info.description:
Every ATProto XRPC call this project actually makes, grouped by which file makes it. Two independent PDSs are involved: the node's self-hosted PDS (domain agents' own identity) and bsky.social (Synthesis's identity, since it's the only component with a human-facing audience). See CONTEXT.md for the architecture behind why these are separate.

Security note: leave the *_app_password variables empty here and set real values in a Postman Environment instead (Environments aren't meant to be committed to git; this collection file is). Never fill in real passwords in the collection itself.

Request chaining: the two 'Create Session' requests have test scripts that auto-populate the corresponding *_access_jwt (and *_did, if blank) collection variables from the response, so everything downstream in that PDS's folders just works once you've run Create Session once.

variable.description: The node's self-hosted PDS. Set via ATPROTO_PDS_URL in ATProto/publisher.py.
Auto-filled by Create Session if left blank; hardcoded here since it's already public knowledge (see Synthesis/publishers.json).
BSKY_APP_PASSWORD — fill in via a Postman Environment, not here.
Auto-populated by 'Create Session' (Node PDS). Not used anywhere in this codebase — see 'Refresh Session' request notes.
Synthesis's PDS. Set via BSKY_PDS in Synthesis/publisher.py — genuinely bsky.social, not self-hosted, since this is the one identity with a human audience.
Auto-filled by Create Session if left blank.
BSKY_SYNTH_APP_PASSWORD — fill in via a Postman Environment, not here.
The custom lexicon every domain and synthesis record uses.
Public did:plc resolution service — see CONTEXT.md 'DID resolution' section for what this does and doesn't guarantee.
Fill in after running 'List Records' once — used by 'Get Record'.

request.description: Confirms the PDS is up. Public, unauthenticated. Used manually throughout ATProto/pds/README.md's setup verification.

One-time call — mints the node's did:plc. No auth needed (works without an invite code since PDS_INVITE_REQUIRED=false). This is the curl command from ATProto/pds/README.md step 11; recent bluesky-social/pds images don't ship pdsadmin, so this plain XRPC call is the actual mechanism, not a CLI tool.

This is the OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials (ROPC) grant, RFC 6749 §4.3 — handle + password submitted directly, no redirect. 'identifier' can be a handle or a DID; ATProto/publisher.py sends the handle. Returns accessJwt (short-lived, ~2h) and refreshJwt (long-lived) plus the account's did. The test script here auto-populates node_access_jwt/node_refresh_jwt/node_did for every request below.

item.name: Refresh Session (reference only — unused in this codebase)

request.description: NOT called anywhere in ATProto/publisher.py or Synthesis/publisher.py — both re-authenticate via Create Session fresh on every cron invocation instead, since each run is a short-lived process well inside the accessJwt's ~2h lifetime. Included here for reference: this is how a long-lived client would mint a new accessJwt without re-sending the password, using the refreshJwt as the Bearer token (not the accessJwt — note the different header value from every other authenticated request in this collection).

Exact shape from build_watershed_record() in ATProto/publisher.py. Note dischargeCfs/gageHeightFt are strings, not numbers — ATProto records are DAG-CBOR, which has no float type in its data model, so numeric fields pulled from SQLite REAL columns are stringified before publishing (see _atproto_safe()). The PDS enforces repo == the DID your accessJwt session belongs to — you cannot write into a repo you're not authenticated as, even with a valid session.

body.raw:
{
  "repo": "{{node_did}}",
  "collection": "{{lexicon}}",
  "record": {
    "$type": "{{lexicon}}",
    "observedAt": "2026-07-02T02:00:25.443751Z",
    "nodeId": "napa-node-01",
    "observationType": "{{lexicon}}#weather",
    "summary": "Extreme wind event continues with sustained elevated winds and dry conditions.",
    "flagged": true,
    "flagReason": "",
    "agentModel": "claude-haiku-4-5",
    "weather": {
      "stationId": "KAPC",
      "activeAlerts": [],
      "temperature_f": "62.6",
      "humidity_pct": "72.401374699018",
      "wind_gust_mph": "95.3"
    }
  }
}

request.description: Exact shape from build_weather_record() in ATProto/publisher.py.

Exact shape from build_aqi_record() in ATProto/publisher.py. pm25Aqi/ozoneAqi are real integers here (not stringified) — they come from a SQLite INTEGER column, not REAL, so no DAG-CBOR float issue applies.

Same ROPC login, against bsky.social instead of the node's self-hosted PDS — Synthesis has its own separate identity/account, deliberately distinct from the node's, since it's the only component that also posts to the public Bluesky app layer for a human audience.

body.raw:
{
  "repo": "{{synth_did}}",
  "collection": "{{lexicon}}",
  "record": {
    "$type": "{{lexicon}}",
    "observedAt": "2026-07-02T22:55:00Z",
    "nodeId": "napa-synth-01",
    "observationType": "{{lexicon}}#synthesis",
    "summary": "Napa Valley's extreme wind event continues to show genuine moderation, with wildfire smoke persisting at Moderate PM2.5.",
    "flagged": true,
    "flagReason": "Maintaining moderate fire and air quality risk pending confirmed resolution.",
    "agentModel": "claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "synthesis": {
      "fireRisk": "moderate",
      "floodRisk": "none",
      "airQualityRisk": "moderate",
      "overallRisk": "moderate",
      "synthesisDid": "{{synth_did}}",
      "domainsObserved": ["watershed", "weather", "aqi"],
      "reasoning": "Full cross-domain reasoning goes here — this is the field that made the ATProto record the complete, publicly auditable source of truth instead of just what fits in a 300-grapheme Bluesky post. See CONTEXT.md's Viewer discussion for why this was added."
    }
  }
}

request.description: Exact shape from build_synthesis_record() in Synthesis/publisher.py. Notice observationType uses #synthesis, distinguishing this from the three domain observation types even though it's the same lexicon collection — that's how subscriber.py, the Viewer, and this collection's List Records requests all filter synthesis records out of domain-record listings (and vice versa).

This is the human-facing side — a completely different lexicon (app.bsky.feed.post, Bluesky's own, not our custom one) so it renders in any Bluesky client. Built by BlueskySession.create_post() in Synthesis/publisher.py, called right after the lexicon record above so the viewer link facet can point at the just-created record's URI. Byte offsets in facets are UTF-8 byte positions, not character positions — see the comment in create_post() about why. This is also the request that hits Bluesky's 300-grapheme post limit, which is what started the whole Viewer thread in this project.

item.name: List Records — Node PDS domain observations

request.description: No Authorization header — repo data is public by protocol design, which is the whole point of 'data bound to the DID, portable, federable.' This is exactly what Synthesis/subscriber.py's fetch_from_publisher() calls, and what you ran manually via curl earlier. Response is paginated via a cursor field; add &cursor=... to page through more than one page. The test script grabs the most recent record's rkey into example_rkey for the Get Record request below.

item.name: Get Record — by repo + collection + rkey

request.description: Fetches exactly one record by its rkey (the last path segment of its at:// URI). This is what the Viewer's getRecord() calls to load the specific record a ?uri= link points at. Also unauthenticated.

Same call, different repo/PDS — this is what the Viewer's getLatestSynthesisUri() calls (with SYNTHESIS_DID hardcoded client-side) to auto-load the current advisory when you land on the Viewer with no ?uri= param.

Not technically an ATProto XRPC call — this is the separate did:plc directory service (operated by Bluesky PBC) that every did:plc identity depends on for resolution. Returns a DID document; look at the 'service' array's '#atproto_pds' entry for serviceEndpoint — that's how resolvePds() in Viewer/index.html and resolve_pds() in Synthesis/subscriber.py find out which PDS a given DID actually lives on, without hardcoding it. See CONTEXT.md's 'DID resolution — the plc.directory dependency we didn't remove' section for the full discussion, including what happens if this service ever goes away.
Same call for the synthesis identity — resolves to bsky.social's serviceEndpoint, since that's genuinely where this account's PDS is.
